leaders.notes: Founded Liberty University (as Lynchburg Baptist College) in 1971 and served as president until his death in office on May 15, 2007. Start year predates this index's 1996+ cutoff but is included for continuity since he was still sitting president in 1996.

Succeeded his father on Jerry Falwell Sr.'s death in 2007. Resigned August 24-25, 2020 amid a personal scandal and was placed on indefinite leave shortly before; received a $10.5M severance settlement. No major subsequent institutional leadership role has been reported; he later sued Liberty University over the terms of his departure.

leaders.priorTitle: Chairman of the Board of Trustees (retired Senior Pastor, Anchorage Baptist Temple)
leaders.notes: Named acting/interim president August 10, 2020 after Falwell Jr.'s ouster; continued in the role (titled interim/acting throughout, per Wikipedia listed as the university's fifth president) until Dondi Costin's arrival in mid-2023. Retired to president emeritus status.

Appointed sixth president, assuming office July 1, 2023 (inaugurated October 2023); first Liberty president not named Jerry. Retired U.S. Air Force major general and former Chief of Chaplains before his higher-ed career; led Charleston Southern University 2018-2023 immediately prior.

Left LMU in 2009 to become president of Tusculum College, serving there until retiring in 2017; there is a one-year gap (2001-2002) between Bishop's and Moody's listed terms not accounted for in the sources found.

Returned for a brief roughly three-month stint as interim president in summer 2005, bridging Steve Flatt's departure and Randy Lowry's arrival.

leaders.notes: 17th president, September 2005-September 2021; launched the university's first doctoral programs and established six colleges. Transitioned to chancellor after stepping down from the presidency.

leaders.notes: 18th president and first woman CEO of Lipscomb, an alumna ('96); previously served Lipscomb as SVP and dean of its College of Education before her state cabinet post as Tennessee's education commissioner under Gov. Bill Haslam.

Named interim president following Bernard Knoth's abrupt resignation in October 2003, serving until Kevin Wildes took office in 2004.
16th president, 2004-2018; announced retirement in 2017 with a national search producing his successor, Tania Tetlow, in 2018.

leaders.notes: 17th president and the first woman and first lay person to lead Loyola New Orleans, inaugurated November 2018. Announced in February 2022 she would step down that summer to become president of Fordham University.
